worst: A: rice study's main finding (0.00-0.23% editing at 179 off-target sites; no genome-wide SNV/indel increase; 'highly specific') is dropped, leaving only a 'pegRNAs need fewer homologous sites' caveat
worst_summary_quote: the authors concluded that pegRNAs with homology to fewer off-target sites are needed for high specificity
worst_page_quote: did not induce significant numbers of genome-wide pegRNA-independent off-target edits in plants
reader_gets_wrong: A reader may think the rice study found specificity depended on better pegRNA design rather than that prime editors were found highly specific with very low off-target rates.
notes: Usable pages: CAS news and PMC10120949 only (genengnews, PubMed, Springer, Yonsei empty or blocked; patents are PDFs). B: closing line 'sources agree... pegRNA design is the main lever' overgeneralises across unlike sources. C (maybe from unfetched pages): patent figures (3 of 16, 97% vs 0.7%), PE-tag claims, Yu et al. Cell 2023. <0.1% sPE/tPE figure matches PMC. Opus adds a hedge that results are abstracts/unverified and that the patent is not peer-reviewed, which Haiku lacked. No absolute prime editing efficiency given.
